title: Evolve the diagram: every new box answers a named flaw
caption: Start with the simplest thing that works, then add one box per unmet requirement or number.

steps.text: v1 is client → service → database. It meets the functional requirements and nothing else.
Hold it against the non-functional requirements and your estimates: peak QPS, data size, latency, availability.
Something fails, e.g. 17k reads/s on one database. Add exactly one box that fixes it (a cache) and say which number forced it.
Then check the new version again. New boxes bring new flaws.
Nothing unmet: stop drawing and move to the deep dives. Extra boxes without a reason count against you.

scenarios.name: Leaderboard loop
scenarios.summary: Two turns of the loop on the leaderboard: each one names a number that fails and adds the one box that fixes it.

steps.text: Check: "rank of one player among 5 M under 100 ms" fails; COUNT(*) scans millions of rows.
Add a sorted set for ranks: "because rank must be O(log n)".
Check again: writes now go to two stores and the sorted set could miss updates. Add a queue and an updater worker, and say why.
Third check: nothing unmet. Stop at v2 and go deep on ranking.

scenarios.name: Risk: boxes, no reasons
scenarios.summary: Adding Kafka, microservices and a cache "for scale" without a failed number is over-engineering: interviewers mark it down.

steps.text: v1 already has eight boxes: queue, cache, three services, two databases.
The check is skipped: no number says any of them are needed.
Asked "why the cache?", the only answer is "for scale". The "say why" step can't be done.
Mitigation: start from three boxes and let each failed requirement earn the next one.
